entry.title: This Is What Mystical Writing Feels Like (Dean Koontz Interview)

media:group.media:title: This Is What Mystical Writing Feels Like (Dean Koontz Interview)
media:group.media:description:
Learn more about Alpha School at ⁠https://go.alpha.school/howiwrite
Dean Koontz has written more than a hundred novels and sold over 500 million copies of his books. This is my second time having him on the show. The first time, we discussed writing practices, routines, and rituals: the standard topics we cover on How I Write.
This time was different. We explored the supernatural, mysticism, and how to cultivate a sense of wonder both in life and on the page.
The vibe of this conversation felt like two old friends sitting in a cabin, discussing life, the world, and the craft of writing.

entry.title: The Writing Habits Behind 50 Million Books Sold (Jodi Picoult Interview)

media:group.media:title: The Writing Habits Behind 50 Million Books Sold (Jodi Picoult Interview)
media:group.media:description:
Learn more about Alpha School at ⁠https://go.alpha.school/howiwrite
Jodi Picoult is on the show today, and she has published 30 novels and sold more than 50 million copies of her books. For a while, she was writing a book a year!
What I admire so much about her is how much fun she clearly has with her craft. Her research sent her ghost hunting and up to Alaska to visit Eskimos. She also gets so invested in her stories that she literally hears her characters speaking to her.
How does she do it? How did she manage to write a book a year? That's what this conversation is all about.

entry.title: What Separates Great Writers From Good Ones (Robert Greene Interview)

media:group.media:title: What Separates Great Writers From Good Ones (Robert Greene Interview)
media:group.media:description:
Pre-order Robert Greene's latest book here: https://sites.prh.com/lawofthesublime
Learn more about Alpha School at ⁠https://go.alpha.school/howiwrite
Robert Greene is on the show today, who's famous for books like The 50th Law and The 48 Laws of Power. How does he write books that so many people want to read? How has he written books so compelling that people literally want to steal them? That’s what we discuss in this conversation.
What I admire so much about Robert, and the reason I love spending time with him, is that he has devoted decades to the craft of writing. You can feel it in his presence. He has labored and labored over his work, and now he is out with a new book called Sublime, which he wrote after suffering a stroke that left him paralyzed on the right side of his body.
This book is his magnum opus. It is a departure from the standard Robert Greene fare, moving into something new, transcendent, and supernatural. An attempt to describe the indescribable. This conversation is beautiful and deep, and I think you will like it.
